method: Research checked October 26, 2026. Published hours, restrictions and dated reports are not live conditions or guaranteed water clarity.
Map pins can be approximate entrances or service anchors. Use the named public destination and access notes for navigation. Distances are straight-line miles.
Saved choices and Done dates belong to this browser. Export a backup to move them. This edition starts with no personal visits or selections.
Lodging quotes are for the dates shown and one adult, with taxes unverified. Recheck the actual dates, guest count and final price before booking.

Beaches and rating snapshots checked October 27, 2026. Matching Google and AllTrails place scores have equal weight. Review counts remain separate; trail-only scores are identified. Expand Ratings & reviews for listing names, capture methods and sources.

places.name: Blue Hole Spring / Jug Spring, Ichetucknee
places.area: North end of Ichetucknee Springs State Park
places.navigationDestination: Ichetucknee Springs State Park North Entrance, 8294 SW Elim Church Road, Fort White FL
places.experience: Snorkel over a deep cyan spring opening, with fish and turtles and the cave entrance beginning about 40 feet below the surface. Blue Hole, also called Jug Spring, is the deep-hole experience beside Ichetucknee's shallower headspring. Reach it on the roughly half-mile woodland trail from the North Entrance. Strong flow makes this an experienced-swimmer stop; entering the cave requires the appropriate cave or cavern qualification.

places.name: Garden of Eden Trail, Apalachicola Bluffs and Ravines Preserve (Alum Bluff)
places.navigationDestination: Garden of Eden Trail trailhead, Garden of Eden Road off State Road 12, 1.6 miles east of Bristol, FL 32321
places.experience: Hike 3.75 miles round trip from longleaf sandhills down a steep slope forest, across a seepage stream in a steephead ravine, and back up to the Alum Bluff overlook of the river floodplain. places.experience: Separate seasonal experience inside existing entry blue-spring-orange-city (he has done the swim). Walk the spring-run boardwalk from the St. Johns River up toward the boil and watch manatees resting in the run; seasonal manatee programs run in winter. Optional two-hour narrated St. Johns River nature cruise from the park concession, and Hontoon Island is next door.

places.experience: Paddle the state-designated trail: CR 419 bridge to the forest headquarters launch is 8 miles, and the full trail runs 19 miles to the SR 46 bridge on the St. Johns. places.name: Crystal River guided manatee swim tour (Bird's Underwater, Kings Bay)
places.navigationDestination: Bird's Underwater Dive Center, 320 NW US Highway 19, Crystal River, FL 34428
places.experience: A guide takes a small boat from the shop's own dock on Kings Bay to wherever the manatees are that morning (often King Spring or the Three Sisters area), then gets in the water with you for passive observation. Wetsuit, mask and snorkel are included. Take the 6 a.m. boat: they are usually first off the dock, before the crowds.

conditions.summary: Tours run daily. From Nov 15 to Mar 31 the refuge closes its manatee sanctuaries to all waterborne activity, so guides snorkel outside the roped areas. One outfitter says that when the Crystal River reading drops below 62.7 F, the swim moves outside the springs into the surrounding Three Sisters area. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

places.name: University of Florida Bat Houses
places.area: UF campus, Museum Road across from Lake Alice, Gainesville, Alachua County
places.navigationDestination: UF Bat Houses, Museum Road (across from Lake Alice), Gainesville, FL
places.experience: Get there before sunset, sit on the benches along the Museum Road fence line or across by Lake Alice, and watch the western sky as the bats stream out 15-20 minutes after sunset. Bats may swoop close to catch insects.

conditions.summary: Viewing is open, but UF says bats emerge on calm evenings above 65 F; cold, wind or rain keeps them in. Late-November evenings are often cooler, so emergence is hit or miss. Colony numbers fell after the 2024 hurricanes (WUSF, Dec 2024); current count not verified. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

places.name: Forest Road 33 (Orange Hammock Road, the old FR 65) roadside dispersed sites
places.experience: A wide crushed-gravel forest road running north from SR 40 along the west edge of the Juniper Prairie Wilderness, with sandy pull-offs in sand pine scrub on the west side. The first usable pull-offs are within about a mile of the highway, which makes it roughly five minutes from Juniper Springs; Silver Glen and Salt Springs are further up SR 19. No toilets, water, tables or signal.

conditions.summary: Dispersed camping is prohibited forest-wide during general gun season, Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027. Legal again from Jan 11, 2027. Nearest legal sites for the trip: Hopkins Prairie Campground ($16) or Juniper Springs Campground ($38). (source dated read 2026-11-12)

camp.sedanNote: Forest Service road data lists FR 33 as crushed aggregate or gravel, maintenance level 3 'suitable for passenger cars', open all year for its full 11.1 miles; Florida Rambler drove it in a Honda Civic ('adequate, although I could hear sand scraping the bottom'). The numbered side spurs (33-1.4, 33-2.4, 33-3.8) are native sand rated high-clearance, so stay on the main road's pull-offs.
camp.carSleepingNote: FWC brochure: 'Camping is allowed throughout the year. Use of trailers or self-propelled camping vehicles is prohibited except in designated campgrounds.' Neither FWC nor the Forest Service says whether sleeping inside a passenger car counts.
camp.stayLimit: 14 days in a 30-day period
camp.huntingNote: Ocala WMA general gun season is Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027 in the Pipeline, Hopkins Prairie and Lake Delancy units (Church Lake Unit on the far west edge: Nov 14-22 and Nov 28 - Dec 6). FWC 2026-27 brochure: 'During the general gun season, camping is prohibited, except in designated campgrounds and Juniper Prairie Wilderness.' Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' So roadside dispersed camping here is NOT legal on any night of Nov 21 - Dec 8, 2026; it was legal in late October. Deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange; wear orange yourself if you walk outside a campground.

Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' This is a designated campground, so it stays legal for the whole trip. Hunters will be on the surrounding forest roads; deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange, and it is sensible to wear orange on trails outside the campground.
camp.gateHours: Campground gate is locked at 6 p.m. during Daylight Savings (Mar - Oct) and 4 p.m. (Nov - Mar). Campers who check-in after the gatehouse is closed must visit the Gatehouse the next morning to complete their check-in to their site. Failure to do so will lead to a 'no show' charge to your reservation and potential forfeiture of site.
camp.directions: From the intersection of Florida Highways 19 and 42, go east on Highway 42 toward Paisley. Drive approximately 6 miles and turn left at the entrance to Clearwater Lake Recreation Area.
camp.showerAccess: Shower facility listed. Hot water, operating hours and access without a booking are unconfirmed.

places.name: Edward Medard Conservation Park
places.navigationDestination: 6140 Turkey Creek Road, Plant City, FL 33567
places.experience: Rent a canoe or kayak at the entry station ($25 for up to four hours, then $10 an hour, tax included) and paddle the reservoir, or walk the boardwalk to the observation platform. A 3-mile trail runs through pine flatwoods and hardwood hammock. The 1.4-mile Singing Bluffs trail (primitive, rated strenuous) is on this season's county Hiking Spree list, and Audubon birding hikes are held here. It is a reservoir, not a spring, so there is no clear-water swimming.

places.name: Ichetucknee Springs Campground (private)
places.area: Fort White, by the Ichetucknee North Entrance
places.navigationDestination: 245 SW Breckenridge Lane, Fort White, FL 32038
places.experience: An old-Florida private campground under big oaks, with bathrooms, showers and a game room. Primitive tent sites have no power or water at the site (there is community water around the grounds and outlets in the main building around the clock); tent sites with power are 20-amp. Regular rates for two people: $30 primitive, $40 tent with power, $50 RV, plus tax and a one-time $5 booking fee. Thanksgiving rates apply Thursday to Saturday: $40 primitive and $50 tent with power. Booking is by phone only, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., (386) 497-2285. Cash, Venmo, Zelle, Apple Pay and Google Pay have no fee; cards add 3%. The rules do not mention sleeping in a car, so ask when you call. It is not part of the state park.

places.name: Eagle's Nest Sink (Chassahowitzka WMA)
places.area: Northwest of Weeki Wachee, Hernando County
places.navigationAddress: Chassahowitzka Wildlife Management Area main entrance, Rattlesnake Camp Road, Weeki Wachee FL
places.experience: From above it looks like a green, marshy pond in a swamp; the show is underwater. A wooden boardwalk and stairs go down into the sink, with benches on the dock, an information sign, picnic tables and a vault toilet at the parking area. Scuba diving needs a state registration on file before you dive, and by long-standing practice only full-cave divers dive here; it has a long record of deaths. That registration covers scuba only: no rule found bans swimming or freediving, but visibility swings from gin-clear to near zero with rainfall, and there is no shallow safe section.

conditions.summary: State wildlife agency pages read November 23, 2026: scuba registration required, vault toilets at the Eagles Nest parking area, $3/$6 daily fee, general gun season Nov 7 - Jan 3. Water clarity not checked. (source dated 2026-11-23)

places.name: Buford Spring (Chassahowitzka WMA)
places.area: North of Weeki Wachee, Hernando County
places.navigationAddress: Chassahowitzka Wildlife Management Area main entrance, Rattlesnake Camp Road, Weeki Wachee FL
places.experience: A boardwalk leads from the trailhead through the swamp to a small spring pool that drops past 150 feet. In dry spells the water can be close to unlimited visibility; after heavy rain it goes tannic or green. The best light is around 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. on a clear day. The swimming area is small; it is a freediving and scuba site more than a place to hang out. The water in front of the dock is dangerously shallow: do not jump in. Scuba needs the same state registration as Eagle's Nest; freediving is not covered by that rule.

For your own benefit, please be sure the company that you are renting from has a CUA with Gulf Islands National Seashore. Gates close at sunset; registered campers arriving late; the entrance code for the gate is in your confirmation email.
